newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port union plans four-hour stoppage.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port union plans four-hour stoppage.

text.p: The Ceylon Mercantile Union (CMU), the biggest in the Colombo port, said on Wednesday it planned a four-hour work stoppage on Thursday.

CMU leader Bala Tampoe told Reuters they called the stoppage to discuss opposition to government plans to allow the Peninsula & Oriental Shipping Co (P&O) set up a container terminal at the port, south Asia's trans-shipment hub.
The government says it has not yet completed a deal to give the port's Queen Elizabeth Quay, one of its two main quays, to P&O to set up a container terminal.
Tampoe said they planned a meeting of their entire 6,000 members from 12.30 pm to 4.30 p.m. (0600-1000 GMT) on Thursday.
A Sri Lanka Ports Authority spokesman said he expected the stoppage would have little impact on the port's operation as other unions among a total workforce of 16,000 had agreed to work.
The CMU was planning further industrial action to oppose a deal, Tampoe said.
"If they stop work, the port can't function," Tampoe said. "Although it is not a strike, it has the same effect."
